Naamah
NAY-uh-muh
proper noun
Hebrew Naamah, “pleasantness” or “sweetness” — a town of Judah in the low country (the Shephelah); distinct from the women of the same name.

Biblical Definition

Naamah, “pleasantness,” was a town of Judah in the Shephelah, the low rolling country between the hills and the coast, listed in a cluster of the valley cities: “And Gederoth, Bethdagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah” (Josh 15:41). It is not to be confused with Naamah the daughter of Lamech (Gen 4:22) nor with Naamah the Ammonitess, mother of Rehoboam; this is a place, not a person. The name is a sweet one, and the Shephelah was indeed a pleasant and fruitful region compared with the dry south, well-watered and set with vineyards and grain. The town preaches the pleasantness of the LORD’s portion. David, surveying his own lot, sang, “The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage” (Psa 16:6), and every faithful Israelite could say the same of the land God gave. Yet the truest pleasantness is not the fatness of the Shephelah but the favour of God Himself, in whose presence is fulness of joy. Naamah, a pleasant town among the vineyards, is a small figure of the far greater sweetness of communion with the God who giveth His people a goodly heritage and Himself for their exceeding great reward.

Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Judah in the fruitful low country, “pleasantness” (Josh 15:41); a figure of the pleasant heritage God gives, and of the sweetness of communion with Him.

NAAMAH, a town of Judah in the Shephelah (low country).

Named once, with Beth-dagon and Makkedah (Josh 15:41).

The name means “pleasantness” or “sweetness.”

Distinct from the women named Naamah in Scripture.

A figure of the pleasant heritage and communion God gives.

Key Scripture

Josh 15:41 — "And Gederoth, Bethdagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with their villages:"

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

Josh 21:45 — "There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass."

Josh 23:14 — "And, behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth: and ye know in all your hearts and in all your souls, that not one thing hath failed of all the good things which the LORD your God spake concerning you; all are come to pass unto you, and not one thing hath failed thereof."

Modern Corruption

A pleasant town of the Shephelah; it recovers the truth that God’s portion is pleasant, and the sweetest heritage is communion with Him.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. A town named once raises no modern quarrel. The only confusion to guard against is mistaking this place for one of the women named Naamah; the Shephelah town is a distinct entity, a pleasant place among the valley cities of Judah.

The principle to recover is that the LORD’s portion is truly pleasant, and Himself the sweetest of all. David rejoiced, “The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage” (Psa 16:6). Yet the psalm rises higher, to the LORD Himself as the portion of the soul. Earthly pleasantness fades, but in God’s presence is fulness of joy and pleasures for evermore; the believer’s truest Naamah is the favour of God.

A town of Judah in the fruitful low country, “pleasantness”; a figure of God’s pleasant heritage and the sweetness of communion with Him.
